summary_en: Turns certain nouns into adjectives meaning 'giving the feeling of N' (사랑 -> 사랑스럽다 'lovable', 자연 -> 자연스럽다 'natural').
ja_diff_note: Like 男らしい or 大人っぽい it means 'having the quality of N', but it never carries the hearsay or guessing らしい (that is -나 보다 / -대요). It is also lexical: only set nouns take it, so you can't attach it freely the way you can with っぽい.
notes: Noun + 스럽다, conjugated as a ㅂ-irregular: 자연스러워요, 사랑스러운 아기, 걱정스러웠어요.
Common ones: 자연스럽다 (natural), 사랑스럽다 (lovable), 부담스럽다 (too much, burdensome), 어른스럽다 (mature), 촌스럽다 (tacky), 걱정스럽다 (worrying).
Related: -답다 (true to being N: 남자답다) and -적 (Sino 的).

examples.ko: 이선 씨, 한국어 발음이 정말 자연스러워요.
examples.en: Ethan, your Korean pronunciation is really natural.
examples.ja: イーサンさん、韓国語の発音がとても自然ですね。

examples.en: A really expensive present feels like a bit much.
examples.ja: あんまり高いプレゼントはちょっと気が重いな。

drills.prompt_en: 준수 is the youngest, but sometimes he's really mature.
drills.explain_en: ㅂ-irregular: 스럽 + 어 -> 스러워; 어른스러운 is a noun modifier and can't end the sentence.

drills.prompt_en: I want to speak naturally, like a Korean.
drills.explain_en: To modify the verb 말하다 you need the adverb form -스럽게.

drills.prompt_ko: 어머님이 반찬을 너무 많이 주셔서 좀 ___.
drills.prompt_en: Your mom gave me so many side dishes, it's a bit much.
drills.explain_en: 부담스럽다 = feeling burdened, and the ㅂ-irregular gives 부담스러워; 부담하다 means 'to bear a cost'.
Before a noun, ㅂ-irregular 스럽 + 은 becomes 스러운.
